result.topic_en: Corollary 2 on the existence of residues proper to the formula x^{P-1}-1, a scholium explaining why it must be proved that for every prime divisor P there is a geometric progression whose residues are complete, and the start of the theorem stating this.

38. Quicunque numerus primus pro diuiſore P

N 2 1, a,

items.quote: Hinc ſemper eiusmodi dantur numeri diviſore P minores, qui caſus formulae $x^{P-1}-1$ proprios exhibent, ita, vt iidem caſus nulli formulae inferiori conueniant.
items.english: Hence there always exist numbers less than the divisor P which give cases proper to the formula x^{P-1}-1, such that these same cases belong to no lower formula.

items.quote: vbi imprimis ante omnia eſt oſtendendum, quicunque numerus primus pro diuiſore P accipiatur, ſemper eiusmodi progreſſiones geometricas $1, a, a^2,$ $a^3, a^4$ etc. exhiberi poſſe, vnde ſeries reſiduorum completae reſultent
items.english: where first of all it must be shown that, whatever prime number is taken as divisor P, geometric progressions 1, a, a^2, a^3, a^4 etc. can always be exhibited from which complete series of residues result, in which all numbers less than P occur before the same order of residues returns.

items.quote: Quicunque numerus primus pro diuiſore P accipiatur; ſemper eiusmodi progreſſio geometrica
items.english: Whatever prime number is taken as the divisor P, there is always a geometric progression 1, a, ... (theorem continues on next page).
